note: Checker verdicts for the 2026-11-06 findings (batch 7.5), keyed by finding id; see docs/audit/README.md

ORD-01.title: Double submit at checkout places two Orders from one Cart (no idempotency)
ORD-01.fixed_by: c800e71 (7.1): placeOrder calls lockCart(input.owner, tx) (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on carts) before getCart at src/modules/ordering/internal/place.ts:192; lockCart at src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts:193; clearCart runs in the same transaction (place.ts:306). Test tests/db/place-order.test.ts:267 'places one Order when the same Cart is submitted twice at once' asserts one Order, one cart_problem and pickup_window_usage drinks 2.
ORD-01.problem: Fixed in 7.1: the second placement on the same Cart waits on the Cart row lock and then finds the Cart empty.
ORD-01.reasoning: Default Prisma isolation on Postgres is READ COMMITTED (no isolationLevel set anywhere in src), so after the lock wait getCart takes a new snapshot and sees the lines the first transaction deleted. The second call returns cart_problem, so no second Order, Order Code or Capacity is taken. The db test runs two placeOrder calls at once against the real test database.
ORD-01.corrections: The audit's preferred nonce-and-redirect was not built. The second request gets 'Something in your Cart changed. Check your Cart.' (checkout/actions.ts:44) instead of the existing Order, so after a pre-hydration double tap, where the browser keeps the second response, the Customer can land on that message with an empty Cart while their one Order exists. That is a small UX follow-up (low), not the duplicate-Order bug.

ORD-02.title: Signing in with a Guest Cart crashes the first page (concurrent mergeGuestCart: P2002 / P2025)
ORD-02.fixed_by: c800e71 (7.1): currentCartOwner wrapped in React cache() (src/modules/cart/internal/session.ts:24); mergeGuestCart locks the Guest Cart first and returns if it is gone (src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts:214). Test tests/db/cart.test.ts:151 runs two merges at once.
ORD-02.problem: The hk_cart cookie is still never cleared after a merge, so every page a signed-in Member opens (the header CartButton calls currentCartOwner) still opens a merge transaction (BEGIN, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, COMMIT) for up to 30 days. The crash is gone, but this part of the finding's impact remains as wasted database round trips.
ORD-02.fix: Check for a Guest Cart with a plain findUnique on the token hash before opening the merge transaction, so the common case costs one read. Or run the merge once from a Server Action or the sign-in callback that also deletes the hk_cart cookie.
ORD-02.reasoning: The P2002/P2025 race is closed: the second merge blocks on the Guest Cart row lock and, once the first commits and deletes the row, the SELECT FOR UPDATE returns no rows and it returns early; cache() also dedupes the header and page call within one request. grep shows hk_cart is only read or set (session.ts:25, 41, 44), never deleted, so the per-request transaction described in the impact still happens.
ORD-02.corrections: Main problem (error page on first render after sign-in) is fixed; only the leftover per-request merge transaction remains.

ORD-03.title: Late paid webhook after Expire/Cancel is silently ignored: Customer charged, no Order, no log, no in-app refund
ORD-03.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): recordPaymentEvent locks the Payment row and accepts a paid event unless already paid or refunded (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-118); a refused transition(paid) becomes paid_late and is refunded after the commit (src/modules/ordering/internal/webhook.ts:52-64); closeCheckout calls expireCheckout first and keeps the Payment open if the provider refuses (payments.ts:131-144). Test tests/db/payments.test.ts:187 'refunds a payment that lands after the Order expired'.
ORD-03.problem: If the automatic late refund fails at the provider, refundPayment puts the Payment back to paid, the webhook only logs 'refund by hand' and answers 200 (so the provider never retries), and refundOrder still refuses Expired Orders and unpaid-then-Cancelled Orders (paidAt is null), so no Manager can refund it in the app. Meanwhile the Order page tells the Customer 'The refund is on its way.'
ORD-03.fix: Let refundOrder accept a closed Order whose Payment is paid (status expired or cancelled with payment.status paid) and show those Orders on /manage/orders with the Refund button. Add a db test where the provider refund throws for a late payment.
ORD-03.reasoning: The common path is fixed and tested: a late paid event stores providerPaymentId, the Order stays Expired, and a Refund row with actor 'webhook' is written. The fallback branch (webhook.ts:65-70) is the only place the old 'no record, no in-app refund' outcome survives, and it needs both a late payment and a failed provider refund. Test Mode only (ADR 0006), so low.
ORD-03.corrections: No test covers closeCheckout keeping the Payment pending when expireCheckout throws, or the refund-failure branch.

ORD-11.title: Parallel queries inside the placement transaction (Promise.all on tx) trigger pg's deprecation; breaks on pg@9
ORD-11.fixed_by: b6209ec (8.8): getOrderingDay runs its four reads in sequence when the client is not db (src/modules/cafe/internal/ordering-day-db.ts:17-34); every other Promise.all in src uses db, not a transaction client.
ORD-11.problem: Fixed in 8.8: reads on a transaction client now run one after another.
ORD-11.reasoning: The only Promise.all that received a tx was getOrderingDay; it now branches on client === db. A grep of every Promise.all in src shows none over tx or client. The roadmap reports Vitest warnings going from 10 to 0.
ORD-11.corrections: The suggested guard that turns the pg warning into a test failure (process.on('warning')) was not added, so a new Promise.all on tx would only show as a warning again (info).

PAY-01.title: Paid webhooks for a Payment that is no longer pending are silently dropped: Customer charged, Order stays Expired/Cancelled/Placed, no refund path
PAY-01.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): paid events are accepted for pending, failed and expired Payments under a row lock (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-118); a retry after a failed attempt pays the Order (tests/db/payments.test.ts:203); a payment after Expire or Cancel is refunded automatically (webhook.ts:52-64, test payments.test.ts:187); closeCheckout marks expired only after the provider confirms (payments.ts:131-144).
PAY-01.problem: When the automatic refund of a late payment fails at the provider, the Payment stays paid on an Expired or Cancelled Order, the only trace is a console.error, the webhook answers 200 so nothing retries, and refundOrder refuses those Orders, so there is still no in-app refund path for that case. The Customer is told the refund is on its way.
PAY-01.fix: Make refundOrder accept a closed Order whose Payment is paid and list such Orders with a Refund button on /manage/orders (or retry the refund from the daily cron). Cover the provider-refund failure with a db test.
PAY-01.reasoning: Every reproduction in the finding now works: the failed-then-paid case pays the Order (test line 203), the after-expiry case refunds (test line 187), and closeCheckout no longer pre-marks expired. The residual is the same narrow refund-failure fallback as ORD-03.
PAY-01.corrections: A Payment is still marked failed on one failed event, as the audit advised against, but a later paid event is now accepted from failed, so the harm is gone.

PAY-02.title: Payment rows are updated read-then-write with no status guard: closeCheckout can overwrite paid with expired, and concurrent paid events clobber providerPaymentId
PAY-02.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): recordPaymentEvent reads the Payment with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-100) and ignores a paid event once paid or refunded (line 110); closeCheckout's write is updateMany guarded on status pending or failed (payments.ts:141-144). Test tests/db/payments.test.ts:215 'keeps the first payment when two paid events arrive for one checkout'.
PAY-02.problem: Fixed in 7.2: Payment writes are serialized by a row lock and guarded on status.
PAY-02.reasoning: Under READ COMMITTED, closeCheckout's guarded updateMany re-checks status after waiting on the webhook's lock, so it cannot overwrite paid. The second paid event finds status paid and returns ignored, so providerPaymentId keeps the first id and no false 'paid after the Order closed' log is printed. refundPayment's claim is also a guarded updateMany.

ID1-03.title: No Staff management: the Manager invite, role changes, removal and session revocation exist only as SQL
ID1-03.fixed_by: a8d191e (8.5): /manage/staff (src/app/manage/staff/*) with setRole and endSessions in src/modules/identity/internal/staff.ts (role by email, last Manager kept under a lock, sessions ended on losing a role, 'Sign out everywhere', both audited); ADR 0005 update records that there is no invite. Tests tests/db/staff.test.ts:42-97 and tests/e2e/manage.spec.ts.
ID1-03.problem: Resetting a Staff member's Second Factor after a lost phone is still a DELETE FROM two_factors run in the database, so on the live demo only someone with Neon access can do it. ADR 0014 accepts this, but it is the one item of the finding's list still outside /manage.
ID1-03.fix: Add a 'Reset Second Factor' action per person on /manage/staff that deletes their two_factors row and sessions and writes an audit entry. Or leave it, since ADR 0014 already records the SQL route as the decision.
ID1-03.reasoning: Role grant, change, removal (back to Member) and session revocation now exist in /manage, gated by requireStaff('manager') and re-checked in setRole. Roles are read from the database on every request (identity/internal/session.ts:18-21), so a demoted Barista loses /bar at once. grep finds no two_factor code outside the generated client, and docs/06 still gives the SQL.
ID1-03.corrections: The invite itself was dropped by decision (ADR 0005 update, line 32), which the audit offered as an alternative. Note: Better Auth's cookieCache (maxAge 5 min, identity/internal/auth.ts:19) means 'Sign out everywhere' without a role change can take up to 5 minutes to stop a /bar session.

SEC1-01.title: Unauthenticated arbitrary file write: an Event Sign-up email becomes a file path in the mail outbox
SEC1-01.fixed_by: c6ad0b6 (7.3): send() keeps only [\w@.+-] of the address in the file name (src/modules/notify/internal/outbox.ts:59), so '/' and '\' become '_' and path.join cannot leave data/mail. Test src/modules/notify/internal/outbox.test.ts 'keeps the file inside data/mail whatever the address holds' with 'a/../../../<marker>@example.com'.
SEC1-01.problem: Fixed in 7.3: no address can steer the outbox file outside data/mail.
SEC1-01.reasoning: With separators replaced, the file name is one path segment ('<stamp>-<hex>-<sanitised>.txt'); dots alone cannot traverse inside a single segment, and the stamp prefix rules out Windows device names. The sink is shared, so every caller is covered.
SEC1-01.corrections: The Sign-up and Inquiry schemas still use the hand-written regex, not z.email() (src/modules/content/internal/signups.ts:42-50, inquiries.ts:22-30); the only remaining effect is the mailto parameter injection tracked under SEC2-01. A 220+ character address would also give ENAMETOOLONG locally; the Sign-up action catches send errors, so it is harmless.

SEC1-03.title: vercel.json migrates the production database from every Preview build
SEC1-03.fixed_by: c6ad0b6 (7.3): vercel.json buildCommand is 'if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" = "production" ]; then prisma migrate deploy; fi && next build'; docs/06-SETUP.md section 9 (line 130) explains it.
SEC1-03.problem: Fixed in 7.3: Preview builds no longer run prisma migrate deploy.
SEC1-03.reasoning: This is exactly the audit's first suggested fix, and section 9 was updated. A failed production migration still fails the build, because the if statement returns the migrate exit status before &&.
SEC1-03.corrections: Previews still share the production database; that wider point is the remainder of SEC2-04 and DATA-05.

SEC1-05.title: No error.tsx or global-error.tsx: errors show Next's unbranded page with no Concept Notice
SEC1-05.fixed_by: a304e60 (8.2): src/app/(site)/error.tsx, src/app/manage/error.tsx and src/app/bar/error.tsx render ErrorPanel (src/components/error-panel.tsx: Try again via retry(), a way on, the digest) inside layouts that carry the Concept Notice; src/app/global-error.tsx brings its own document, palette script and Concept Notice.
SEC1-05.problem: Fixed in 8.2: branded error pages with the Concept Notice exist at every level.
SEC1-05.reasoning: The retry prop matches Next 16.4.3's error.md (retry is stable since 16.3). The (site) footer, manage/layout.tsx and bar/layout.tsx contain the 'Hoshikopi is a concept cafe' notice, and global-error.tsx includes it directly.

SEC1-06.title: Event Sign-ups are unverified and unprotected: Seats can be hoarded and arbitrary addresses emailed
SEC1-06.fixed_by: 5d3bc2d and f78d858 (8.7): Sign-ups wait for an email link and hold Seats only 30 minutes (heldSignups, src/modules/content/internal/signups.ts:15-19); 2 Sign-ups per IP per Event per day on top of 10 tries an hour (src/app/(site)/events/[slug]/actions.ts:23, 36, 65-73); confirm and cancel by button on /events/[slug]/signup/[id]; the email no longer carries the typed name (src/modules/notify/index.ts:74-114). Tests tests/db/signups.test.ts:92-138.
SEC1-06.problem: The Inquiry form, which the finding also named, still has only 5 per IP per hour, with no honeypot or minimum fill time, so attacker text still floods /manage/inquiries. A Manager still cannot remove a fake Sign-up that was confirmed from an address the sender controls.
SEC1-06.fix: Add a hidden honeypot field and a minimum fill time to the Inquiry and Sign-up forms and drop submissions that fail them. Add an audited Manager action on /manage/events/[id] to remove a Sign-up.
SEC1-06.reasoning: Seat hoarding with made-up addresses now expires after 30 minutes, the per-visitor cap limits one IP to 8 Seats per Event per day, guests can cancel, and the email carries no attacker text. grep finds no honeypot or fill-time check anywhere, the inquiry action is unchanged apart from the shared rate limit, and grep finds no eventSignup delete reachable by a Manager.
SEC1-06.corrections: The cafe contact address is on the reserved hoshikopi.example domain, so on the demo inquiries reach the logs and /manage/inquiries, not a real inbox. The per-visitor key is the IP from x-forwarded-for, which is spoofable off Vercel (a separate rate-limit finding).

SEC1-07.title: A payment that lands after its Order expired is silently 'ignored', not logged as paid_late
SEC1-07.fixed_by: b59c16f (7.2): recordPaymentEvent matches pending, failed and expired Payments (src/modules/payments/internal/payments.ts:96-118); webhook.ts:52-64 turns paid_late into an automatic full refund (refunded_late, Refund row, actor 'webhook') and logs 'refund by hand' if that fails. Test tests/db/payments.test.ts:187 now expects refunded_late, Payment refunded with providerPaymentId, and one Refund row.
SEC1-07.problem: Fixed in 7.2: a payment after expiry is refunded automatically, and logged if the refund fails.
SEC1-07.reasoning: The exact fix the finding proposed (match expired Payments, refund through refundPayment, change the test) is in place and tested.
SEC1-07.corrections: The narrow refund-failure branch has no in-app follow-up; it is recorded under ORD-03 and PAY-01.

SEC1-22.title: iCalendar text escaping keeps lone CR and control characters; folding can split emoji
SEC1-22.fixed_by: 2711031 (8.6): src/lib/calendar.ts text() uses /\r\n|\r|\n/g and strips C0 controls except tab plus DEL; fold() iterates code points and counts UTF-8 bytes against 75. Tests src/lib/calendar.test.ts:36 (lone CR and control characters) and :44 (folds at 75 bytes without splitting a character). content/internal/calendar.ts now delegates to it.
SEC1-22.problem: Fixed in 8.6: escaping and folding follow RFC 5545.
SEC1-22.reasoning: for...of walks code points, so a surrogate pair is never cut, and the byte count matches the RFC's octet limit, with continuation lines counting their leading space.

SEC2-01.title: Event Sign-up email becomes a file path in the email outbox: anyone can write .txt files anywhere on the server
SEC2-01.fixed_by: c6ad0b6 (7.3): same fix as SEC1-01, the shared sink sanitises the file name (src/modules/notify/internal/outbox.ts:59) and outbox.test.ts covers a traversal address.
SEC2-01.problem: Sign-up and Inquiry emails are still checked only by /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/, which accepts 'x@y.z?cc=a%40b.c&body=hi', and the Manager pages put that value unencoded into href='mailto:...', so a visitor can add cc and body parameters to the Manager's reply. The file-write part of this finding is fixed.
SEC2-01.fix: Validate with z.email() in signups.ts and inquiries.ts, as checkout does. Wrap the address in encodeURIComponent in both mailto links, as inquiries/page.tsx:183 already does.
SEC2-01.reasoning: Same root problem as SEC1-01 (raw recipient in the outbox file name), and that part is gone. This finding also reported the mailto injection from the same permissive regex and recommended z.email(); neither changed. Checked: the regex accepts the injection string (node test) and both links interpolate the raw email. The Manager sees the prefilled cc before sending, so impact is low.
SEC2-01.corrections: It is the same problem as SEC1-01 for the file write; the mailto injection is an extra point only this finding made.

SEC2-02.title: One anonymous visitor can book out an Event's seats with fake, unverified Sign-ups
SEC2-02.fixed_by: 5d3bc2d and f78d858 (8.7): email confirmation with a 30-minute hold (signups.ts:15-19, 92-149), a per-IP cap of 2 Sign-ups per Event per day undone past the limit (events/[slug]/actions.ts:23, 65-73), and confirm or cancel by link. Tests tests/db/signups.test.ts:92-138, tests/e2e/content.spec.ts.
SEC2-02.problem: A Manager still has no way to remove a Sign-up, so Seats taken by confirmed fake Sign-ups (an address on a catch-all domain the sender controls, 8 Seats per IP per Event per day) stay taken. The roadmap's 8.7 note says this was left out.
SEC2-02.fix: Add a 'Remove' button per Sign-up on /manage/events/[id] that deletes it under the Event row lock, writes audit(), and refreshes the content tag. Cover it with a db test.
SEC2-02.reasoning: The main attack (unverified addresses filling an Event within a minute) is closed: unconfirmed Sign-ups free their Seats after 30 minutes, and one IP gets at most 2 successful Sign-ups per Event per day. grep finds eventSignup deletes only in the guest's own cancel (signups.ts:243) and the expired-wait cleanup (signups.ts:125), none for a Manager.
SEC2-02.corrections: Two IPs can still hold a 12-Seat Event for 30 minutes unconfirmed, or permanently with catch-all addresses; that is the accepted ceiling of a per-visitor cap.

SEC2-04.title: Preview deployments run prisma migrate deploy against the shared production database
SEC2-04.fixed_by: c6ad0b6 (7.3): vercel.json runs prisma migrate deploy only when VERCEL_ENV is production.
SEC2-04.problem: Setup step 3 still sets DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL and BETTER_AUTH_SECRET for Production and Preview alike, so a preview's unreviewed code reads and writes the live demo data and shares the auth secret with production. A Neon branch per preview is left as the owner's switch and nothing in the repo shows it is on.
SEC2-04.fix: Turn on the Neon integration's branch per Preview deployment (or set Preview-only DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL), and give Preview its own BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. Change step 3 of docs/06-SETUP.md to say which variables are Production only.
SEC2-04.reasoning: The title's problem (migrations from previews) is gone. The finding's other points, the shared secret and a shared database contrary to ADR 0004, are unchanged: docs/06 line 134 still reads 'for Production and Preview', and line 130 says previews share the production database unless the integration is turned on.

SEC2-14.title: The ICS text escaping misses a lone CR
SEC2-14.fixed_by: 2711031 (8.6): src/lib/calendar.ts text() replaces /\r\n|\r|\n/g with \\n; test src/lib/calendar.test.ts:36.
SEC2-14.problem: Fixed in 8.6: a lone CR is escaped.
SEC2-14.reasoning: Exactly the suggested regex, with a test. This is a subset of SEC1-22.

DATA-05.title: Preview deploys run `prisma migrate deploy` against the production database, though ADR 0004 promises separate preview databases
DATA-05.fixed_by: c6ad0b6 (7.3): vercel.json migrates on Production builds only.
DATA-05.problem: ADR 0004 still says Neon holds production and preview databases with branches per preview, but none is set up: docs/06 sets the same Neon URLs for Production and Preview and calls the preview branch the owner's switch. Previews therefore still run against production data, and a preview of a schema change runs new code on the old schema.
DATA-05.fix: Turn on the Neon Vercel integration's branch per preview and set DIRECT_URL for Production only, as the audit suggested. Otherwise add an update to ADR 0004 saying previews share the production database and never migrate it.
DATA-05.reasoning: The migration half is fixed exactly as suggested. The ADR contradiction this finding added on top of SEC1-03 remains: ADR 0004 is unchanged since 2026-10-30, and docs/06 line 130 makes preview databases conditional.
DATA-05.corrections: Repeats SEC1-03 for the migration (fixed) and overlaps SEC2-04 for the shared database.

PERF-01.title: Signing in with a guest Cart crashes the first /checkout or /cart render (concurrent guest Cart merges)
PERF-01.fixed_by: c800e71 (7.1): currentCartOwner is wrapped in React cache() (src/modules/cart/internal/session.ts:24), so one request merges once; mergeGuestCart locks the Guest Cart row first (src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts:214 via lockCart at :193), so a second merge from another request finds it gone instead of hitting P2002/P2025. Test: tests/db/cart.test.ts:151 "merges once when two requests sign in with the same Guest Cart at once"; e2e tests/e2e/members.spec.ts:13 signs in with a Guest Cart and opens /checkout.
PERF-01.problem: Fixed in 7.1: the merge runs once per request and concurrent merges serialise on the Guest Cart row lock.
PERF-01.reasoning: It is the same problem as ORD-02 (interim audit line 51, "concurrent mergeGuestCart: P2002 / P2025"). The 7.1 fix covers both causes: two calls in one render (now deduplicated by cache()) and two requests at once (now serialised by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the Guest Cart, then an early return when it is gone). The db test runs two merges with Promise.all against the real database.
PERF-01.corrections: The audit's 'merge once per sign-in' part is only half done: the hk_cart cookie is still never cleared after a merge (no write to it besides cartOwnerForWrite), so every signed-in render still runs a small transaction with a SELECT FOR UPDATE that finds nothing. That cost belongs to PERF-07, not this crash.

PERF-02.title: Bar Screen poll version ignores makeNext and Prep Time, so Scheduled Orders stay under "Later today"
PERF-02.fixed_by: 94609ff (7.4): the barBoard version now includes the Prep Time and the count of make-next Orders, and 8.4 (11c6363) added the Busy Mode end time (src/modules/ordering/internal/bar.ts:105-109). Test: tests/db/bar.test.ts:105 "changes its version when a Scheduled Order becomes make-next" and :163 for Busy Mode.
PERF-02.problem: Fixed in 7.4: a version change follows the clock crossing windowStart minus Prep Time, and a Prep Time change.
PERF-02.reasoning: It is the same problem as the 7.4 Bar Screen fix (Scheduled Orders move to New on time). makeNext only turns from false to true as time passes, so the due count rises whenever an Order turns due without a row change. Prep is computed from settings plus the queue, so a Manager's Prep Time edit changes the version too. A Busy Mode that ends on its own clears day.busy, which is also in the version.

PERF-03.title: Signed-out Bar Screen poll follows a redirect to the sign-in HTML (55.6 kB), JSON parsing throws and the board freezes silently
PERF-03.fixed_by: 94609ff (7.4): /api/bar checks currentStaff("barista") and answers 401 JSON with no redirect (src/app/api/bar/route.ts:15-17); poll() stops on 401 and shows the "You're signed out, so the board stopped updating. Sign in again" alert; the JSON parse is guarded with .catch (src/app/bar/bar-screen.tsx:146-151, 257-265). Test: tests/e2e/bar.spec.ts "the Bar Screen says it stopped when its session ends (audit, 7.4)". Probed on :3300: GET /api/bar?v=x signed out returns 401 application/json, 18 bytes {"signedOut":true}.
PERF-03.problem: Fixed in 7.4: a signed-out poll gets an 18-byte 401 and the board says it stopped.

PERF-04.title: Menu photos uploaded in a production build are not served (written to public/ at runtime)
PERF-04.fixed_by: d7289e1 (5.4 Blob): storeMenuPhoto puts photos into the Vercel Blob store when BLOB_STORE_ID or BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN is set (src/modules/menu/internal/photo.ts:62-75); next.config.ts:28-34 allows *.public.blob.vercel-storage.com for next/image; unit test src/modules/menu/internal/photo.test.ts with the Blob client mocked.
PERF-04.problem: Without a Blob token, storeMenuPhoto still writes to public/menu at runtime, and `next start` (the e2e server on 3100 and the local production server on 3300) lists public/ only at startup, so an upload made there is a 404 until a restart. No test uploads a photo and fetches it, and the first real upload on the live site is still listed as left to do in 5.4.
PERF-04.fix: Serve the local fallback from a Route Handler (or a directory outside public/), or make storeMenuPhoto refuse the upload in production without a Blob token. Then do one real upload on the live demo and record that the image request returns 200.
PERF-04.reasoning: The deployed demo (Vercel) is the case that mattered, and it now goes to Blob, where writeFile could not work. The fallback path is unchanged from the finding, and Next 16.4.3 still scans the public folder only once at startup in production (filesystem.js:263-265).
